title: Geometric stalks of a sheaf of modules of finite type are finitely generated
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] which is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] and $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ the stalk of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], a $\Lambda$-module by $\lambda\cdot(\text{germ of }s)=\text{germ of }\lambda s$. Then $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. More precisely: if $u:U\to Y$ is etale, $\mathcal G|_U$ is generated by the global sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal G(U)$ and $\bar u$ is a geometric point of $U$ with $u\circ\bar u=\bar y$, then $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is generated by the germs of $s_1,\dots,s_n$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u)$.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5); the stalk statement is not stated in Stacks for the etale site (agent-formulated; compare the proof of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, where a finite type module is generated near x by sections s_1, ..., s_n, and the proof of Lemma 093N (1), where a section is locally a Lambda-combination of the generators)

proof.text: *The stalk as a $\Lambda$-module; germs.* For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal H$ on $Y_{\Et}$ the stalk $\mathcal H_{\bar y}$ is the colimit of the groups $\mathcal H(V)$ over the pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; write $\mathrm{germ}_{(V,\bar v)}:\mathcal H(V)\to\mathcal H_{\bar y}$ for the coprojections, so that $\mathrm{germ}_{(V',\bar v')}(a|_{V'})=\mathrm{germ}_{(V,\bar v)}(a)$ for every morphism $h:(V',\bar v')\to(V,\bar v)$ of pointed neighbourhoods ($a|_{V'}=\mathcal H(h)(a)$). The index category is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]: for two objects $(V_1,\bar v_1),(V_2,\bar v_2)$ the fibre product $(V_1\times_YV_2,(\bar v_1,\bar v_2))$ is an object mapping to both by the projections. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (1), applied with $R=\mathbf Z$ and with $R=\Lambda$ to $\mathcal H=\mathcal G$ (each $\mathcal G(V)$ a $\Lambda$-module through $\iota_V:\Lambda\to\Lambda_Y(V)$, the restriction maps being $\Lambda$-linear), every element of $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is $\mathrm{germ}_{(V,\bar v)}(t)$ for some pointed neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ and some $t\in\mathcal G(V)$, the colimit in abelian groups and in $\Lambda$-modules is the same set of germs, and its $\Lambda$-module structure is $\lambda\cdot\mathrm{germ}(s)=\mathrm{germ}(\lambda s)$, the one of the statement; every $\mathrm{germ}_{(V,\bar v)}$ is $\Lambda$-linear.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *The first assertion follows from the 'more precisely' clause.* As $\mathcal G$ is of finite type there are an etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ (jointly surjective, etale) and, for each $i$, finitely many sections $s_{i1},\dots,s_{in_i}\in\mathcal G(U_i)$ generating $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] (with $T=Y$, the family $(u_i)$ and the geometric point $\bar y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]) there are $i\in I$ and a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_i$ with $u_i\circ\bar u=\bar y$. The 'more precisely' clause (steps 3 to 7), applied to $U=U_i$, $s_j=s_{ij}$ and $\bar u$, shows that $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is generated by the $n_i$ germs $\mathrm{germ}_{(U_i,\bar u)}(s_{ij})$, so it is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. From now on let $u:U\to Y$, $s_1,\dots,s_n$ and $\bar u$ be as in the 'more precisely' clause, and let $x\in\mathcal G_{\bar y}$; we show $x=\sum_jc_j\,\mathrm{germ}_{(U,\bar u)}(s_j)$ for some $c_j\in\Lambda$.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *A representative over $U$.* By step 1, $x=\mathrm{germ}_{(V,\bar v)}(t)$ for a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$ and $t\in\mathcal G(V)$. Let $V'=V\times_YU$ with $\bar v'=(\bar v,\bar u)$, an object of the neighbourhood category mapping to $(V,\bar v)$ and to $(U,\bar u)$ by the projections [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], and $t'=t|_{V'}$; then $x=\mathrm{germ}_{(V',\bar v')}(t')$ (step 1). The projection $p:V'\to U$ is etale, as the base change of the etale morphism $V\to Y$ along $u$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; so $(p:V'\to U)$ is an object of the localised site $Y_{\Et}/U=U_{\Et}$ (its structure morphism to $Y$ is $u\circ p$, the structure morphism of $V'$), $t'\in\mathcal G(V')=(\mathcal G|_U)(V'\to U)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type], and $p\circ\bar v'=\bar u$.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *The generators locally.* Let $\varphi:(\Lambda_Y|_U)^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ be the morphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y|_U$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ sending the $j$-th basis section $e_j$ to $s_j$; it is an epimorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y|_U$-modules by hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (1), applied to the site $U_{\Et}$ and the sheaf of rings $\Lambda_Y|_U$, the functor forgetting the module structure is additive and preserves cokernels; in the abelian categories of sheaves of modules and of abelian sheaves a morphism is an epimorphism iff its cokernel is $0$, so the underlying morphism of abelian sheaves of $\varphi$ is an epimorphism of $\Ab(U_{\Et})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] (with $X=U$), applied to the section $t'$ over the object $V'\to U$ (step 3), there are a covering $\{q_k:W_k\to V'\}_{k\in K}$ in $U_{\Et}$ and sections $g_k\in(\Lambda_Y|_U)^{\oplus n}(W_k)$ with $\varphi_{W_k}(g_k)=t'|_{W_k}$. By clause (2) of the same lemma limits, hence finite direct sums, are computed sectionwise, so $g_k=(\lambda_{k1},\dots,\lambda_{kn})$ with $\lambda_{kj}\in\Lambda_Y|_U(W_k)=\Lambda_Y(W_k)$, i.e. $g_k=\sum_j\lambda_{kj}\,e_j|_{W_k}$, and by $\Lambda_Y(W_k)$-linearity of $\varphi_{W_k}$ and compatibility with restriction $t'|_{W_k}=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_{kj}\,s_j|_{W_k}$ in $\mathcal G(W_k)$ (here $s_j|_{W_k}$ is the restriction along $p\circ q_k:W_k\to U$). For $n=0$ this says $t'|_{W_k}=0$.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *Lifting the geometric point to one member of the covering.* The family $\{q_k:W_k\to V'\}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $\bar v'$ is a geometric point of $V'$; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] (with $T=V'$) there are $k\in K$ and a geometric point $\bar w$ of $W_k$ with $q_k\circ\bar w=\bar v'$. Then $W_k\to V'\to Y$ is etale (an object of $U_{\Et}$ is an object of $Y_{\Et}$ by composing with $u$, as in the localised site), $(W_k,\bar w)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar y$, and $q_k$, $p\circ q_k$ are morphisms of pointed neighbourhoods $(W_k,\bar w)\to(V',\bar v')$ and $(W_k,\bar w)\to(U,\bar u)$ (since $p\circ q_k\circ\bar w=p\circ\bar v'=\bar u$).

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *Making the coefficients constant.* We construct, for $m=0,\dots,n$, a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W^{(m)},\bar w^{(m)})$ with a morphism $r_m:(W^{(m)},\bar w^{(m)})\to(W_k,\bar w)$ and $c_1,\dots,c_m\in\Lambda$ with $\lambda_{kj}|_{W^{(m)}}=\iota_{W^{(m)}}(c_j)$ for $j\le m$, where $\iota$ is the canonical map from the constant presheaf to $\Lambda_Y$. Start with $(W^{(0)},\bar w^{(0)})=(W_k,\bar w)$, $r_0=\mathrm{id}$. Given $m<n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-ring-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] (with $T=Y$, the object $W^{(m)}$ and $\lambda=\lambda_{k,m+1}|_{W^{(m)}}$): there are a covering $\{W'_l\to W^{(m)}\}$ in $Y_{\Et}$ and $c'_l\in\Lambda$ with $\lambda|_{W'_l}=\iota_{W'_l}(c'_l)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] (with $T=W^{(m)}$) some $W'_l$ carries a geometric point $\bar w'$ over $\bar w^{(m)}$; put $W^{(m+1)}=W'_l$, $\bar w^{(m+1)}=\bar w'$, $c_{m+1}=c'_l$, and $r_{m+1}$ the composite. For $j\le m$ the relation persists, as $\iota$ is a morphism of presheaves from the constant presheaf, whose restriction maps are identities: $\iota_{W^{(m)}}(c_j)|_{W^{(m+1)}}=\iota_{W^{(m+1)}}(c_j)$. Put $(W,\bar w)=(W^{(n)},\bar w^{(n)})$, $r=r_n$.

source.place: Definition 03DL (5) and Definition 03DE (4), (5) (finite type, generated by finitely many sections); the argument is the one of Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01B8 (modules.tex, lemma-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) for ringed spaces, transposed to geometric stalks on the small etale site (agent-written)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Restricting the identity of step 4 along $r:W\to W_k$ gives $t'|_W=\sum_j\iota_W(c_j)\,s_j|_W=\sum_jc_j\,s_j|_W$ in $\mathcal G(W)$, the $\Lambda$-module structure of $\mathcal G(W)$ being given by $\iota_W$ (step 1). The composites $(W,\bar w)\to(W_k,\bar w)\to(V',\bar v')$ and $(W,\bar w)\to(W_k,\bar w)\to(U,\bar u)$ are morphisms of pointed neighbourhoods (steps 5, 6), so by step 1 (compatibility of germs with restriction and $\Lambda$-linearity of $\mathrm{germ}_{(W,\bar w)}$) $x=\mathrm{germ}_{(V',\bar v')}(t')=\mathrm{germ}_{(W,\bar w)}(t'|_W)=\sum_jc_j\,\mathrm{germ}_{(W,\bar w)}(s_j|_W)=\sum_jc_j\,\mathrm{germ}_{(U,\bar u)}(s_j)$. As $x\in\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ was arbitrary, the germs of $s_1,\dots,s_n$ at $(U,\bar u)$ generate $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ as a $\Lambda$-module (for $n=0$: $\mathcal G_{\bar y}=0$).

The stalk is (pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber.obj G with its ModuleCat Λ structure, the canonical germwise action.
